title: Two Work Packages write the same two story files and two fragments for legacy RWB-AD-013 on rwb-access
source: Work Package files _work/msr/wp/B-P4-04.md and _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-007.md (B-P4-04 lists the same 'Write only' paths 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/RWB P4 AD013 APP Roll back a rule or reference version v1.md and RWB P4 AD013 CON Roll back a rule or reference version - contract v1.md, plus _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD013-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD013-CON.json, beside four other legacy keys; B2-P4-007 lists the same four paths alone); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (two slices for legacy RWB-AD-013: RWB-P4-AD013-CON in contract group CG-W4 and RWB-P4-AD013-APP in lane L-P4-G, both wave 4, both release 30 June 2027, both business epic EP08, disposition Split (rework)); _work/msr/status.json (no entry for B-P4-04 and no entry for B2-P4-007); _work/msr/gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl and _work/msr/assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl (the citation set the delivered files carry)
section: Whole story file set of RWB-AD-013 on rwb-access; fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD013-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD013-CON.json
description: The plan carries exactly two slices for legacy RWB-AD-013 on rwb-access (the contract baseline and the application slice), but two Work Packages of the run name them: B-P4-04, which lists RWB-AD-013 beside RWB-AD-012, AD-014, AD-015 and AD-016 with fanout 5 and wrote the AD013 key as part of that fanout, and B2-P4-007, which names the same two story files and the same two fragments alone with fanout 0. The four artefacts are present and complete in the tree: the APP story file is 67,252 bytes and the CON contract file is 36,913 bytes, each with the two header lines of Template and Rules v1 R8.1, a D-RCV-60 change-log row with the tool line T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, the 20 metadata rows of R7.1 in order and matching the two Work Package lines value for value (work type APP and CON with the fixed owner phrase of R5.3, service rwb-access, service epic RWB-SVC-P4, wave 4, business epic EP08, release 30 June 2027 marked (tentative), legacy key RWB-AD-013, disposition Split (rework), build status Not started, patterns DP03, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP13 and DP19, parallel lanes L-P4-G and CG-W4, ready After RWB-P4-AD012-APP and Day 1, H, C, I and X as the Work Package lists them, PRD reference Pending (C1), status Draft (realignment v1)), the 19 section headings of R7.2 in order, tables 12.1 to 12.9 in both files, the Level column of section 16 and no 'As built (monolith)' heading because neither slice is preserved. The APP file carries AC1 of RWB-AD-013 word for word with the origin tag (legacy RWB-AD-013 AC1) and one added Given line for the faked cross-service part, 'Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns version "ENTRY-2026.12" withdrawn to state "ROLLED_BACK" with the previous version "ENTRY-2026.11" in force from 15 December 2026', plus five criteria tagged (new, D-RCV-60); the CON file carries six criteria tagged (new, D-RCV-60); both keep the legacy test case ids TC-AD-013-01, TC-AD-013-02 and TC-AD-013-03 with the Level column, and neither writes an -ITG copy because no integration story is split from this key. The two fragments carry the 28 keys the Work Package lists. Their missing and assumed values are already registered once as CG-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to CG-B-P4-04-AD013-112 with ASM-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to ASM-B-P4-04-AD013-112, and every CG and ASM identifier the four artefacts cite (29 distinct) resolves to a row in a jsonl file of _work/msr/gaps or _work/msr/assumptions, with 0 orphans. The earlier execution left no edit log at _work/msr/editlog/B-P4-04.md and no status entry, so the delivered citation set has no log of its own even though its content is sound. Under root AGENTS.md rule 1 the existing artefacts are kept and this Work Package registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding, so the Gap Register and the Assumption Register are not allocated twice for one legacy key at step D1 and the sibling files RWB P4 AD012, AD014, AD015 and AD016, which cite the same B-P4-04 set, stay consistent with AD013.
evidence: B-P4-04.md title line 'fanout: 5' and its 'Write only' block naming the two RWB P4 AD013 story paths and the two RWB-P4-AD013 fragment paths beside the AD012, AD014, AD015 and AD016 sets; B2-P4-007.md title line 'fanout: 0' and the same four paths alone; split_plan.json slices RWB-P4-AD013-CON (lane CG-W4) and RWB-P4-AD013-APP (lane L-P4-G); status.json: no 'B-P4-04' key and no 'B2-P4-007' key; editlog: no B-P4-04 entry; gaps/B-P4-04.jsonl: 12 rows for this key (CG-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to -112); assumptions/B-P4-04.jsonl: 12 rows for this key (ASM-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to -112); the four artefacts read and checked against R5.5, R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9, with 20 metadata rows, 19 section headings, 12.1 to 12.9, the Level column, the AC origin tags, the three legacy test case ids and 29 resolving CG and ASM citations
proposed: Keep one Work Package per story slice in the plan generator: remove RWB-AD-013 from the B-P4-04 fanout list, or retire B2-P4-007 for this key. At step D1, number CG-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to -112 and ASM-B-P4-04-AD013-101 to -112 once and allocate no second set for B2-P4-007; ask the B-P4-04 execution to write its edit log row so the delivered AD013 citation set has a traceable writer; add a plan-uniqueness check to checks/run_all.py that fails when two Work Package 'Write only' blocks name the same output path.
